dataflow.summary: Authenticated client mutates or deletes user_settings through RLS; service-role AI code reads the resulting state; Pro-model or trial authorization is granted.

attackPath.impact: Unpaid paid-model access, recurring trial access, and unauthorized provider spend.
prerequisites: A valid user account and the public Supabase project endpoint/anon key.

reachability.summary: The browser ships a Supabase client and the policies directly authorize the caller's row, so no edge-function bypass is required.

codeEvidence.explanation: The policy limits row ownership but not protected columns and also permits deletion.
codeEvidence.label: Owner policy permits protected row mutation

codeEvidence.explanation: A caller-controlled far-future grace date is accepted as paid entitlement.
codeEvidence.label: AI trusts client-writable Pro state

codeEvidence.explanation: Deleting the row converts expired access back into trial access.
codeEvidence.label: Missing settings row restores trial

confidence.rationale: The writable RLS policies, later-added entitlement columns, missing-row trial fallback, and authorization reads are directly present in source.

preventiveControls: Column-level privilege restrictions for server-managed fields
findings.remediation: Move entitlements and quota overrides to a service-role-only table, or revoke authenticated writes to protected columns and deletion while exposing narrow preference-only mutations. Treat missing entitlement state as denied or reconstruct it from trusted billing records.
remediationTests: Direct PostgREST updates to subscription_tier, grace_period_ends_at, trial_ends_at, and daily_limit_override are rejected for authenticated clients.
Deleting user_settings is rejected and a missing settings row does not create trial access.
Only trusted billing, promo, and admin paths can change entitlement state.

rootCause.summary: Server-managed billing and entitlement fields share a table whose row-owner policy allows unrestricted client update and deletion.

severity.rationale: Any authenticated user can directly obtain unpaid Pro access or recurring trial access and drive third-party provider spend; exploitation is simple and requires no privileged foothold.

findings.summary: Row-owner policies let authenticated clients update or delete server-trusted subscription state, while both AI functions trust that state for paid-model and trial authorization.
findings.title: Users can self-assign paid entitlements and restore expired trials

validation.counterevidence: The frontend writes only ordinary preferences and trusted service-role paths maintain legitimate entitlements, but direct PostgREST clients are not constrained by frontend behavior.
evidence: Authenticated users can update or delete their own user_settings row.
Billing columns are added later to the same table.
Both AI endpoints derive authorization from those fields.
validation.method: Independent source-backed review of the current authorized repository state.
validation.remainingUncertainty: A separately configured rate_limits row can override forged quota values, but it cannot remove the forged Pro entitlement or the missing-row trial fallback.

dataflow.summary: Anonymous client queries shared_items without .eq(share_code); RLS admits every active row; item_data and metadata are returned.

attackPath.impact: Bulk disclosure of shared cases, chats, sources, titles, creator UUIDs, codes, and timestamps.

CREATE POLICY "shared_items_select_public" ON public.shared_items

dataflow.summary: Authenticated client invokes public RPC directly; definer function reads RLS/auth-protected rows; cross-user telemetry is returned.

attackPath.impact: Disclosure of user UUIDs/emails, platform request/cost/error totals, and individualized/global rate-limit configuration.

reachability.summary: The functions are explicitly granted to authenticated.

codeEvidence.explanation: Clients can bypass the guarded admin edge function and invoke these directly.
codeEvidence.label: Admin RPCs granted to all authenticated users

codeEvidence.code:
SECURITY DEFINER
SET search_path = public
AS $$
BEGIN
  RETURN QUERY
  SELECT ai_requests.user_id, auth_users.email::text AS email, count(*)::bigint AS requests, COALESCE(sum(cost_usd), 0)::numeric AS cost
  FROM public.ai_requests
  LEFT JOIN auth.users AS auth_users ON auth_users.id = ai_requests.user_id
codeEvidence.explanation: Definer rights cross RLS and auth-schema boundaries without checking administrator status.
codeEvidence.label: Definer function reads auth email

confidence.rationale: Function bodies, SECURITY DEFINER declarations, and authenticated grants are all explicit and survive later recreation.

findings.remediation: REVOKE EXECUTE from PUBLIC, anon, and authenticated and grant only service_role, or assert an administrator role inside each function before any privileged read.
remediationTests: Ordinary authenticated RPC calls to all three functions fail.
Admin edge requests still work through service_role.
get_usage_by_user never returns cross-user email data to non-admin roles.

rootCause.summary: Privileged database functions rely on a guarded edge caller but independently grant direct execution to the lower-privileged authenticated role.

severity.rationale: The path reliably discloses cross-user email and enforcement metadata, a material privacy and administrative-boundary failure without write access.

findings.summary: Three administrator-facing SECURITY DEFINER functions have no role check and are explicitly executable by every authenticated user.
findings.title: Security-definer analytics RPCs expose emails, costs, and rate limits to ordinary users

validation.counterevidence: The admin edge function correctly authenticates and checks admin status, but direct RPC invocation bypasses it.
evidence: All three functions are SECURITY DEFINER.
Explicit authenticated grants exist.
get_usage_by_user joins auth.users.email.
validation.method: Independent source-backed review of the current authorized repository state.
validation.remainingUncertainty: PostgreSQL PUBLIC defaults may make exposure broader than authenticated; the explicit authenticated grant is sufficient for this finding.
validation.summary: Confirmed no auth.uid/user_roles check and no later revocation; the replacement email function re-grants authenticated execution.

attackPath.impact: Arbitrary-target entitlement changes, promo-redemption exhaustion, and code-validity oracle behavior.

attackPath.attacker: Ordinary authenticated user controlling body.url and a DNS hostname

dataflow.summary: User URL passes literal-only validation; DNS resolves at fetch time to an internal address; accepted text response is read and returned.

attackPath.impact: Internal-service probing and disclosure of textual internal or metadata responses.
prerequisites: Network reach from the deployed edge runtime to a target.

reachability.summary: The import-source endpoint directly accepts a user URL and performs outbound fetch.

codeEvidence.explanation: DNS records used by the network connection are never checked.
codeEvidence.label: Validation checks hostname text only

codeEvidence.explanation: Connection-time DNS can resolve to an address validation never saw.
codeEvidence.label: Original hostname reaches fetch

confidence.rationale: Validation and fetch are separate and no DNS/address binding exists; the deployment egress prerequisite affects impact, not the source trace.

findings.remediation: Use a hardened egress proxy or resolve all A/AAAA records, reject every non-global address and metadata range, and pin the validated address while preserving TLS hostname verification. Repeat for every redirect.
remediationTests: A hostname resolving to loopback/RFC1918/link-local/ULA/metadata space is rejected.
DNS rebinding cannot change the address after validation.
Every redirect is revalidated and pinned at connection time.

rootCause.summary: SSRF defense validates URL syntax and literal host text rather than the actual connection address.

severity.rationale: The path can expose high-value internal responses, but actual impact depends on the deployed edge network reaching a useful private or metadata service.

findings.summary: The importer rejects private IP literals but never resolves or pins hostnames before fetch, allowing a public or rebinding hostname to connect to internal addresses.
findings.title: DNS-based SSRF bypasses source-import URL validation

validation.counterevidence: Authentication, banned-user checks, literal private-address blocking, redirect revalidation, and a nominal daily limit reduce exposure but do not close the DNS gap.
evidence: Hostname checks cover literals only.
No DNS lookup occurs.
Accepted response content is returned to the caller.
validation.method: Independent source-backed review of the current authorized repository state.
validation.remainingUncertainty: No repository evidence establishes whether production egress can reach private or metadata services.

attackPath.attacker: Authenticated user controlling an imported public HTTP server

dataflow.summary: User submits controlled URL; headers return before deadline; timer clears; body streams indefinitely or at large size into response.text; regex parser processes it.

attackPath.impact: Invocation retention, memory/CPU exhaustion, and service degradation.
prerequisites: A server that returns accepted content type and a huge or slow body.

reachability.summary: The public import endpoint fetches and parses user-selected servers.

codeEvidence.explanation: fetch resolves on headers, so the timer is cleared before the caller reads the body.
codeEvidence.label: Deadline ends before body consumption

codeEvidence.explanation: The maximum applies later inside normalization, after memory and regex costs.
codeEvidence.label: Entire response is buffered

confidence.rationale: Timeout lifetime, full buffering, and post-buffer truncation are explicit.

findings.remediation: Keep one deadline active through consumption, stream with a byte counter, cancel beyond a conservative maximum, check Content-Length as early defense, and avoid whole-document regex processing above the cap.
remediationTests: A slow body is aborted at the total deadline.
A body above the byte cap is canceled before full buffering.
Compressed or missing-Content-Length responses cannot exceed the streamed limit.

rootCause.summary: Time and output limits are applied around header fetch and normalized output, not during untrusted body streaming.

severity.rationale: An authenticated attacker controlling a public server can reliably retain invocations or exhaust edge memory/CPU, while platform limits may cap the blast radius.

findings.summary: The fetch deadline is cleared when headers arrive, then response.text buffers the entire attacker-controlled body before the 50,000-character output slice.
findings.title: Source importer buffers unbounded response bodies after disabling its timeout

validation.counterevidence: Authentication, content-type checks, and a nominal daily import limit reduce frequency but not per-request memory or duration after headers.
evidence: Controller timeout is cleared in fetchWithTimeout finally.
response.text fully buffers the body.
No Content-Length or stream counter exists.
validation.method: Independent source-backed review of the current authorized repository state.
validation.remainingUncertainty: Runtime-level memory and invocation limits may terminate individual abuse but are not application controls.
validation.summary: Confirmed MAX_CONTENT_CHARS truncates normalized text only after response.text and HTML processing.

attackPath.attacker: Ordinary authenticated user issuing concurrent requests

dataflow.summary: Parallel requests read the same below-limit count; all begin outbound work; only later do their usage rows appear.

attackPath.impact: Quota bypass, multiplied provider spend, SSRF probing, and concurrent resource consumption.
prerequisites: At least one remaining daily slot.
Ability to send a parallel burst.

reachability.summary: All three authenticated edge endpoints implement this ordering.

codeEvidence.code:
const { count, error: countError } = await supabase
  .from("ai_requests")
  .select("*", { count: "exact", head: true })
  .eq("user_id", userId)
  .gte("created_at", todayStart.toISOString());
...
return { allowed: true, limit: dailyLimit, current: currentCount };
codeEvidence.explanation: No slot is reserved before provider work.
codeEvidence.label: AI admits from a non-atomic count

codeEvidence.explanation: Parallel streams remain invisible until completion.
codeEvidence.label: Stream records usage after provider work

codeEvidence.explanation: Concurrent imports all pass before any completion record exists.
codeEvidence.label: Import usage is logged after fetch

confidence.rationale: All three check-then-act sequences and delayed inserts are explicit; no transaction or reservation exists.

findings.remediation: Atomically reserve a per-user/day quota slot in a transactional RPC before any outbound work, share the counter across standard and streaming AI, fail closed on reservation errors, and separately record completion/cost.
remediationTests: A burst at limit-1 admits at most one request.
ai and ai-stream share the same atomic counter.
Import reservations occur before fetch and remain consumed when expensive work began.

rootCause.summary: Quota enforcement uses a non-atomic check-then-act pattern around sensitive work instead of reserving capacity transactionally.

severity.rationale: The race reliably exceeds product limits and can multiply provider/network cost, but practical amplification is constrained by concurrent request and provider capacity.

findings.summary: Import, standard AI, and streaming AI count completed usage rows before expensive work and record usage only afterward, so concurrent requests pass the same stale count.
findings.title: Daily quotas can be overrun through concurrent requests

validation.counterevidence: Sequential completed and caught-error requests are normally logged and eventually counted.
evidence: Standard AI count precedes provider/search calls.
Streaming inserts only after the stream.
Import logs after fetch and parse.
Limiter errors fail open or collapse to zero.

validation.remainingUncertainty: External concurrency limits may reduce but do not eliminate the race.
